From zero state h<b, block 10 decreases H by b-a>0; arbitrarily many zeros increase H by a. gcd(a,b-a)=1 gives a connector to every integer K. For h>=b, a finite run of 1s then 0 enters h<b. Thus all zero states communicate and every language pair bridges. The marker omega=10^m1^r0 with am=b(r-1)+1 forces pre-height H=b-1 by its first 10 (H<b) and second ones run (H>=b-1); H=b-1 attains it. Equal start heights of two occurrences imply aN0=bN1 and hence start gaps divisible by a+b, forbidding infinitely many bridge lengths. Nine sample-pair finite regressions passed; proof applies to unbounded parameter and words.

value.rationale: Reyes explicitly asks which frequency shifts are transitive. This result determines the answer for every rational critical density in an entire nontrivial half-interval, a dense infinite family not covered by the known endpoint and upper rational family. The same constructive dynamics exhibits a robust arithmetic nonmixing obstruction, clarifying that transitivity can coexist with nonsoficity and failure of weak specification.
